dlg.maeca.first.0.wants: someone who'll see what she sees
dlg.maeca.first.0.note: Half-voice, level. A flicker of interest on 'Hunter?'. 'They're running.' plain and certain. Dry on 'before you ask'.

dlg.maeca.first.1.note: Quiet and final. 'and so can they' a warning. 'What do you want?' cold.

dlg.maeca.first.2.note: Flat contempt for the bounty. The rule about the problem said plainly. 'What's left of it.' three words, quiet, closed.

dlg.maeca.hub.0.note: Narrator for the cup. 'Say it.' curt.

dlg.maeca.hub.1.note: Calls you hunter as a compliment.

dlg.maeca.driving.0.note: Ground and animals, present tense. A little heat on 'more than a hundred pelts'. Tam's line with quiet sympathy.

dlg.maeca.tracks.0.note: Genuine surprise on 'You saw that?'. Then clinical. 'So. Not bold. Sick.' a verdict.

dlg.maeca.truth.0.note: Contempt for the diggers. 'Days, maybe.' hopeful, guarded.

dlg.maeca.speak.0.note: Instructions, each a rule. A dry edge on 'If he decides wrong, well. Run then.'

dlg.maeca.where.0.note: Plain directions; dry humour on 'fool enough' and 'Rav's piss'.

dlg.maeca.barefoot.0.note: Short and hard. 'They never came.' heavy. 'I prefer it now.' a door closing.

dlg.maeca.signed.0.note: Contempt in 'a good hand'. Then suspicion turned on you.

dlg.maeca.thanks.0.wants: you to know what it means
dlg.maeca.thanks.0.note: Reporting the Hollow, steady. Then the confession, quieter. A long pause. 'Thank you.' barely said; she never says it.

dlg.maeca.cold.0.note: Ice. The last line bitter and quiet.

dlg.maeca.gone.0.note: Each fragment its own blow. The voice never rises; the hurt is in the stillness. 'Get out of my light' through her teeth.

dlg.maeca.gone.1.note: Each fragment its own blow, never raised.

dlg.maeca.cb_burned_roost.0.note: Flat and quiet. 'I was at Ashford.' three words, final.

dlg.maeca.say_calling.2.note: 'Fire's the one thing they all remember.' with a shadow of Ashford.

dlg.maeca.say_calling.3.note: A rare half-smile on 'Pity about the boots.'

dlg.maeca.say_calling.4.note: A rare half-smile on 'Pity about the boots.'

dlg.maeca.invite.0.note: Plain and low, no flirtation. 'Most can't.' dry, a challenge.

dlg.maeca.blind_morning.0.note: Narrator for the frost. Then softer than usual; dry joke on Holloway counting.

dlg.maeca.blind_morning.1.intent: tells you why she never hunts wolves
dlg.maeca.blind_morning.1.wants: you to know, and not to pity her
dlg.maeca.blind_morning.1.note: Narrator for the frost. The story told plainly, present tense feel. 'Kept everything off.' near breaking. A pause. 'That's all of why.' firm. 'Don't make it a story.' a plea disguised as an order.

dlg.maeca.cb_broke_promise.0.note: Three plain statements, cold. Pause. The last line quiet and final.

dlg.maeca.t_maeca.0.note: Deadpan; a grim joke about men on paths.

dlg.maeca.kerchiefs.0.note: 'Some.' Narrator for the cup. 'Fed some of them, once. Buried more.' heavy. 'Ask me about wolves.' a closing door.
